claims.text: FeNiCrCoCu is used as a thin-film protective coating on conventional metals.
Temperature is varied from room temperature to elevated temperatures such as 500°C and 700°C during wear testing.
In situ characterization is performed during temperature-dependent wear testing.
The coating is tested under sliding-wear and abrasive-wear conditions.
A stable oxide layer forms on the FeNiCrCoCu coating as temperature increases.
The surface oxide layer acts as a barrier to wear.
The oxide layer protects the underlying substrate.
Wear resistance increases with increasing temperature.
The increase in wear resistance is caused by formation of a more stable and protective oxide layer.
The proposed temperature boundary extends from room temperature to 800°C.
The proposed loading boundary encompasses sliding and abrasive wear.
Failure of an oxide layer to form and stabilize at elevated temperature would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of wear rate to increase with increasing temperature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted increase in wear resistance normally implies a decrease in wear rate, but the falsification rule says that failure of wear rate to increase would falsify the hypothesis. Thus, the rule requires increasing wear rate even though the predicted outcome implies the opposite.
